applied_items.content:
`change check`, `change verify`, `change accept`, `change finalize` and `change ship` SHALL refuse, before anything is written, a change on a branch that has lost a canonical requirement that no approved `## REMOVED` delta names (#1081). The branch's requirements SHALL be compared with those at a reference commit: the merge-base of `HEAD` and the default branch (`origin/HEAD`, else `origin/main` or `origin/master`), or, when there is no default branch, the change's `base_commit` when that commit is in `HEAD`'s history. A requirement is a `### REQ-` heading outside a fenced block in a `requirements.md` or a legacy `<module>.req.md` under the specs directory or beside a registered spec. A requirement is lost when its id is in such a file at the reference commit and in none of them in the working tree; a requirement that moved to another such file under the same id is not lost. A lost requirement is accounted for when an approved `## REMOVED` requirement item names its id in the delta of this change, of another active change on the branch whose definition approval is valid, or of a change the branch archived after the reference commit. The refusal SHALL name every lost requirement that is not accounted for and the file that held it at the reference commit, SHALL record a refused attempt as other check refusals do (#847), and SHALL name the way out: restore each block from the reference commit (`git show <commit>:<file>` prints it), or remove it on purpose by naming it in a `## REMOVED` delta and approving the change again. When a lost requirement's text is in the working tree under a new id, the refusal SHALL also say that a requirement id is permanent, so a renumbered requirement needs a `## REMOVED` item for its old id. When there is a default branch and Git cannot read the merge-base or a requirements file at it, the refusal SHALL name what could not be read. When there is neither a default branch nor a `base_commit` in `HEAD`'s history, the comparison SHALL be skipped, and `change check` SHALL print one note saying so. `change audit` SHALL report the same refusal for each active change.

Acceptance Criteria
- On a branch whose `requirements.md` was truncated to the change's one added requirement (the starling case), `change check` refuses before writing, names every lost id and its file, and records a refused attempt. `change verify`, `change accept`, `change finalize` and `change ship` refuse the same way, and `change audit` reports it.
- A requirement that an approved `## REMOVED` item removes is not reported, whether the item is in this change, in another active change on the branch, or in a change the branch archived. Nor is a requirement that another change removed on the default branch, once the branch has merged that in.
- A requirement whose block moved to another requirements file under the same id is not reported. A renumbered requirement is reported under its old id, with the permanence hint.
- A deleted requirements file reports every id it held, and a legacy `<module>.req.md` is read like `requirements.md`.
- With no default branch, the change's `base_commit` is the reference. With neither, the check is skipped with a note. With a default branch whose merge-base or file Git cannot read, the check refuses, naming what could not be read.
- These flows pass as before: an ADDED or MODIFIED change, a REMOVED change, a send-back, and a delta rebased under REQ-change-161.

`change ship-status` SHALL list the refusal of REQ-change-169 as a blocker, with the same message, and SHALL NOT report the change ready to finalize while it holds. `change ship --dry-run` SHALL refuse with that message.

Acceptance Criteria
- On the starling-shaped branch, `change ship-status <id>` lists the blocker, reports `ready_to_finalize` false and exits 1, and `change ship <id> --dry-run` refuses with the same message.
- With the lost blocks restored, `ready_to_finalize` is true again.
